label: cor:habiro-expansion-atomic
title: Atomic-braid Habiro expansion: integrality and termination
html:
The algebraic quantum volume of a confined atom \mathfrak{H} admits a q-Habiro expansion:

  \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{alg}}(\mathfrak{H})
  \;=\;
  \sum_{n=0}^N c_n(q) \, (q; q)_n

where the truncation depth N correlates with the number of valence nucleons.

This proposition guarantees that the binding energy formula terminates algebraically when evaluated at a root of unity. The coefficients c_n(q) determine the specific shell contributions. This structure bridges the categorical operator traces to the empirical magic-shell mass phenomenology.

For a knot, the expansion of this shape is Habiro's. The colored Jones polynomials are J_n(q) = \sum_{k \ge 0} c_{n,k}(q)\,H_k(q) with H_k(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm1}] and a knot-independent cyclotomic kernel c_{n,k}(q) = q^{-kn}(q^{n+1};q)_k\,(q^{n-1};q^{-1})_k that vanishes for k \ge n \ge 1, so the sum terminates at each color; at n = 0 the same sum defines an element of the Habiro ring, and replacing q^n by a variable gives an element of the colored Habiro ring [garoufalidis-kashaev-descendants2023, §2.2, eqs. (2)--(4)]. The same paper records a second realization of the colored Jones polynomials through R-matrices at roots of unity built from solutions of the pentagon identity [garoufalidis-kashaev-descendants2023, Abstract and §3]. Both statements concern knot invariants; the application of the expansion to \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{alg}}(\mathfrak{H}) and the reading of N above are made here and are not in that source.
